examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتغل, بيشتغل).

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رئيسية, plural: رئيسيين).

examples.trans: We shut off the main water valve in the cellar.
The main gate is on the quiet street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ركب.

examples.trans: My knees got tired from climbing the stairs.
He sat on the chair to rest his knees.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ركضات.

examples.trans: Great dash to the shop today!
We made it in a quick dash before the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكر, بيسكر).

examples.trans: He said thank you and hung up!
Did you shut off the main water valve?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سنان.

examples.trans: The new brass thread screwed in cleanly.
Be careful not to strip the screw thread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسخن, بيسخن).

The water heated up within five minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شركاء.

examples.text: همه شركاء بالمخبز من عشر سنين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شعلات.

Make sure the pilot light is lit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشغل, بيشغل).

examples.trans: Can we turn the water heater on now?
She started up the coffee machine in the morning.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صمامات.

examples.trans: We fitted a new brass valve on the boiler.
Make sure the valve is tightly shut.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عجلات.

examples.trans: Turn the blue valve wheel slowly.

examples.text: القطار الصغير إله أربع عجلات خشب.
examples.trans: The little train has four wooden wheels.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كشافات.

The flashlight beam is bright and clear in the basement.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماسكة, plural: ماسكين).

He was holding a blue suitcase in his hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مواسير.

Old pipes need maintenance in winter.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: محابس.

examples.trans: I turned off the main water shutoff in the basement.
Open the shutoff tap slowly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مسكرة, plural: مسكرين).

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
The main water valve is shut off now.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مصفاية, plural: مصفايين).

examples.trans: The valve is shut and the line is drained.
Strained mint tea in a glass cup.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ممتازة, plural: ممتازين).

examples.trans: The reading light beside the desk is excellent.
The shower water was hot and excellent!

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نظيفة, plural: نظاف).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نقط.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: وصلات.

examples.trans: Shine the flashlight on the pipe joint.
We tightened the brass fitting with the wrench.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
